title: Your Pokémon save file knows too much about you
dek: Starters, full boxes, abandoned teams and type charts. Twelve questions about the trainer you actually are, with no trivia.

questions.prompt: Professor's lab. Three starters on the table, and your cousin has already grabbed the one you wanted.

options.label: Take the remaining one and pretend it was the plan
Ask if there are more in the back
Pick the one nobody ever picks
Take the one with the best stats, obviously

questions.prompt: Route 1. Tall grass. Your first wild encounter is a small brown bird.

options.label: Catch it. It's tradition
Check its nature before deciding
Run. You have places to be
Catch six and name them after food

questions.prompt: The game gives you one cheat:

options.label: Infinite rare candy
Every Pokémon is catchable

questions.prompt: I'd rather win with my favourites than lose with the best team.
I skip the dialogue and then wonder what happened.
Your rival appears. You are eleven levels under and out of potions.

options.label: Fight anyway. Pride is a strategy
Go back and grind for an hour
Use the one move that shouldn't work
Lose on purpose to see the alternate dialogue

questions.prompt: Naming a Pokémon makes it harder to trade away.
Your PC box, at the end of the game, looks like:

options.label: One perfect team and forty untrained friends
Sorted by type, then by level
Named, costumed, all small and round
Six eggs and a spreadsheet

questions.prompt: There's a rumour about a rare Pokémon behind the power plant.

options.label: Go now, under-levelled
Look up the encounter rate first
Bring thirty of the right ball
Not worth it. You have a save from 2003

questions.prompt: I have opinions about how other people play.
questions.high: I've explained EVs at a party

questions.prompt: A game you can't lose isn't a game.
I've restarted a save because the starter's nature was wrong.

results.name: The Solo Run
results.blurb: You picked one and poured everything into it. The rest of the team is decorative, under-levelled and quietly resentful. It works, mostly, and you'd rather lose your way than win somebody else's.
strengths: Wins in ways that shouldn't work
results.watchOut: The one thing can't cover every gym. Let somebody else take a turn.

results.name: The Dex Filler
results.tagline: If it exists, it goes in the box
results.blurb: You are not playing a game, you are completing a collection. The route is a checklist, the box is alphabetised and a 1% encounter rate is a personal invitation. Your patience is genuinely frightening.
results.watchOut: The last ten entries are never worth the weekend. Go outside with the console.

results.name: The Cute-Only Trainer
results.tagline: A team of small round things
results.blurb: You build a team with your heart and then defend it in arguments. Stats matter less than the way the thing blinks. Your favourites are objectively not the strongest and you have never once cared.
strengths: Makes the game fun for everyone nearby
results.watchOut: Affection is not a type advantage. Carry one sensible Pokémon.

results.name: The Type Matchup Nerd
results.tagline: Has a chart in their head and opinions
results.blurb: You know what's coming before the gym leader does. Your team has coverage, your moves have purpose and your friends ask you what to use against the ghost gym. You are right, and you'd like everyone to notice.
strengths: Turns a hard fight into a maths problem
results.watchOut: Not every conversation needs a matchup. Sometimes just say 'nice team'.

results.name: The Nuzlocke Masochist
results.blurb: You added a rule the game didn't ask for and now it means something. One catch per route, faint means gone, and you will absolutely restart from the beginning. The stakes are fake and the grief is not.
results.watchOut: Not everything in your life needs hard mode. Let one thing be easy.

results.name: The Egg Hatcher
results.blurb: You have spent an evening walking in a circle for a stat. Nobody sees the spreadsheet, the rejected eggs or the twelve hours of preparation — they just see the finished team. You call it optimisation. Everyone else calls it a second job.
results.watchOut: The perfect one is already good enough. Ship it before the game ends.

results.name: The Cutscene Skipper
results.tagline: The story is a loading screen
results.blurb: You're here for the battles. Dialogue gets mashed through, the villain's plan is a rumour and you have somehow reached the eighth gym under-levelled and confused. You still got there first.
strengths: Improvises when the plan is missing
results.watchOut: The bit you skipped is usually the reason the ending works. Read one cutscene.

results.name: The Gen-One Purist
results.tagline: It peaked in 1998 and you can prove it
results.blurb: You've bought the same game four times. Your favourite route is the one you know by heart, your team is the same six and you will explain the original sprite art to anyone who makes eye contact. It isn't nostalgia, you say. It's taste.
strengths: Deep, unironic love for a thing
Knows exactly what made it work
results.watchOut: New things can be good too. Try one without comparing it for an hour.
